title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. A common semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework distinguishes five cases: an isolated dry ferroelectric, a dry ferroelectric connected to a carrier reservoir, a blocking ferroelectric-electrolyte junction, a reactive interface with an external carrier return, and two opposite domains coupled through the solid and electrolyte. Analytical solutions and numerical evaluations connect stationary potentials versus illumination to differential optical spectra and finite light-step responses. We further examine the doping effects on static potentials in all five cases and dynamic photovoltage in the isolated film and a fixed-polarization, bare-surface contacted-film variant. For reactive interfaces, the same framework determines reduction and oxidation rates, their spatial distributions, and accumulated reaction amount. The analysis covers surface charging and photochemical conversion beyond deposition, while retaining the electrical and chemical boundaries that distinguish finite charging from sustained turnover, and explains the observed range of photodeposition morphologies. Finally, this framework builds the theoretical foundation for the modulated photovoltage imaging methods that can readily be realized in SPM under illumination.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive theoretical framework to model light-induced charge dynamics and photochemistry at ferroelectric surfaces. By analyzing five distinct physical coupling scenarios, it quantitatively links charge transport, electrostatics, and interfacial kinetics. The resulting model provides a foundation for interpreting complex photo-response measurements, such as modulated photovoltage imaging.
main_problem: The paper analyzes light-induced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces, aiming to provide a comprehensive quantitative description beyond simple polarization-induced band-bending.
main_result: A generalized semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework is developed that distinguishes five distinct physical cases based on charge return paths, explaining the observed range of photodeposition morphologies.
method: The authors use analytical solutions and numerical evaluations based on a semiconductor transport framework that couples electrostatics, carrier continuity equations, and interfacial kinetic laws.
model_or_system: The system involves ferroelectric surfaces (including domain patterns) interacting with external environments (dry or electrolyte). The model incorporates carrier generation, drift, diffusion, and polarization dynamics ($\Gamma_P\partial_t P = ...$).
key_observables: Stationary potentials vs. illumination, differential optical spectra, finite light-step responses, reduction and oxidation rates, and photovoltage.
important_parameters: Doping effects, polarization state, and the specific boundary conditions defining the charge return path (e.g., isolated film vs. electrolyte contact).
main_assumptions: The analysis explicitly retains the electrical and chemical boundaries to distinguish between transient charging and sustained chemical turnover.

paper_structure: The paper builds a comprehensive framework by analyzing five distinct physical configurations (isolated, reservoir-coupled, blocking junction, reactive interface, coupled domains), deriving governing equations, and applying them to calculate various measurable quantities.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter electrochemistry, the rigorous coupling of electrostatics, charge transport, and reaction kinetics in a non-equilibrium setting shares methodological parallels with open quantum systems modeling where environmental coupling dictates system dynamics.
